clue.text: Fail-or pass by mistake

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass
a lapse is a slip or mistake

explanation.surface: A student fears failing, or scraping a pass only through an error.
explanation.definitionFit: To fail is to break down or give way, as a structure or a business does.

clue.text: Make much of top men joining firm

parts.note: COs are commanding officers, the men at the top
set means firm or solid

explanation.surface: Bosses joining a company are pampered.
explanation.definitionFit: To pamper or indulge someone is to fuss over them.

clue.text: Had fun receiving guidance about an old boat

indicators.note: one word takes in another, so the boat goes inside

parts.note: led means guided
Noah's ark is the ancient vessel

explanation.surface: People enjoyed themselves on being shown round a vintage vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is a link: LED takes in ARK.
explanation.definitionFit: To frolic or play pranks is to have a lark.

clue.text: The dish featured in one of Goya's pictures

indicators.note: the answer appears within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A meal appears in a painting by the Spanish artist.
explanation.definitionFit: A savoury jelly in which meat or fish is set is a cold dish.

clue.text: The American cowboy's topping!

parts.note: topping is read as headgear, the wide-brimmed hat a Western cowboy wears

explanation.definitionFit: This broad-brimmed felt hat is the classic headwear of Western cattlemen.

clue.text: Forced relations with the public on the disruptive side

parts.note: PR is short for public relations

indicators.note: something disruptive throws things into disorder, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Press officers were pushed into work alongside an unruly faction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disruptive' rearranges SIDE into ISED, which follows PR.
explanation.definitionFit: Prised open means levered or forced apart.

clue.text: To do with cash cut exceptionally hard worker opposed

parts.note: re means concerning, to do with
L stands for pounds sterling (librae)

indicators.note: exceptionally means in an unusual way, so these letters are put in an unusual order

parts.note: the ant is the proverbial industrious creature

explanation.surface: A diligent employee objects to a reduction in pay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exceptionally' rearranges CUT to UCT, between L and ANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unwilling is close to being against something.

clue.text: The boards receiving work on the quiet as a result of a strike

indicators.note: one word takes in others, so they go inside

parts.note: the boards is the theatre stage
op is short for opus, a work
p is piano, quiet in music

explanation.surface: The theatre takes on a secret production after an industrial walkout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'receiving' puts OP and P inside STAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: When workers down tools, the halt in work follows.

clue.text: Set off for school in time

parts.note: a date is a point in time
Eton is the famous English public school

explanation.surface: Departing for classes punctually.
explanation.definitionFit: To set off a bomb is to make it explode.

clue.text: Small traveller who's prepared for take-off

parts.note: a tripper is someone on an outing or excursion

explanation.surface: A short holidaymaker is ready for the plane to depart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take-off' suggests an aircraft, but it is the taking off of clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer who removes clothing is ready to take garments off.

clue.text: Innings closed as quickly as possible

definitions.meaning: in cricket, a side is finished when ten batsmen have been dismissed
going flat out, at full speed

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a batting side's innings ends when ten of its eleven batsmen are dismissed.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket innings ends when the whole side is dismissed; going at full effort means maximum speed.

clue.text: Dues demanded when in employment

indicators.note: the letters are worked over into a new order, as demands rework a bill

explanation.surface: Union subscriptions are required while you have a job.
explanation.definitionFit: Something put to work or in service is being employed.

clue.text: Applies for training

definitions.meaning: uses or puts into practice, as one uses a right
drills or workouts done to build skill or fitness

explanation.definitionFit: One uses or wields a power; drills and workouts are practice routines.

clue.text: Fowl may be seen around a river

indicators.note: one piece is found surrounding another, so the river goes inside

parts.note: may means can, be permitted
the Po is Italy's longest river

explanation.surface: A bird can be spotted near some waterway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'be seen around' puts PO inside CAN; 'a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A castrated cockerel fattened for the table is a kind of poultry.

clue.text: This urban area won't get rebuilt

indicators.note: rebuilding puts the same material into a new shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Planners say this city district is never going to be redeveloped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get rebuilt' rearranges the letters of WONT (ignore the apostrophe).
explanation.definitionFit: A settlement larger than a village counts as a built-up place.

clue.text: Upsets superior and goes

parts.note: over means above, superior to
a go is a turn, as in a game

explanation.surface: A boss is upset and leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: To knock something over or reverse it is to capsize it.

clue.text: Wind up a man on the board

definitions.meaning: a current of cold air in a room
a counter in the game played on a chequered board

explanation.walkthrough: 'up' is a link word: a piece is in play (up) on the board.
explanation.definitionFit: A cold current of air indoors; and a playing piece in the board game of that name.

clue.text: Make notes about a point for speech

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: to sing is to produce musical notes
a peak is a pointed summit

explanation.surface: Jotting down remarks about a key point to make a talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make notes' suggests jotting, but it is singing.
explanation.definitionFit: A part involving talk, as in an actor's spoken role, involves utterance.

clue.text: Censure the fool holding one up

indicators.note: holding means containing, one piece inside the other

parts.note: a dunce is a fool

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: Criticise the idiot propping up someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns ONE into ENO, which goes inside DUNCE.
explanation.definitionFit: To condemn publicly is to criticise strongly.

clue.text: Excuse for writing a foreword perhaps

definitions.meaning: a false reason given to hide the real one
a foreword is writing placed before the main body

explanation.definitionFit: A cover story is a false reason; a foreword is writing that comes before the main body.

clue.text: A man in jug

definitions.meaning: a pottery jug moulded as a seated figure in a tricorn hat

explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link between the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: A male first name, also given to the pottery jug shaped like a stout seated figure.

clue.text: The head coppers lunched together

parts.note: coppers are pennies, and P stands for pence
lunched means ate

explanation.surface: The chief of police and his officers had a meal together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coppers' suggests police, but it means copper coins, pence.
explanation.definitionFit: This old word for the crown of the skull is a familiar term for one's head.

clue.text: Stuff with hair-that's for safety reasons

parts.note: to pad is to stuff
a lock is a tress of hair

explanation.surface: Stuffing done with hair to keep things safe.
explanation.definitionFit: A detachable lock with a shackle secures doors and gates.

clue.text: Needy and broken-down artist

indicators.note: broken down means taken apart, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An impoverished painter is in poor shape.
explanation.definitionFit: In dire straits means in difficulty or poverty.

clue.text: Agreement giving rise to no offence-most acceptable

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: taken as written
a sin is an offence
U means upper-class, socially acceptable

explanation.surface: Consent comes from causing nobody offence, which is ideal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'giving rise to' turns NO+SIN+U backwards as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting together in accord means harmony.

clue.text: Concerned with a contest

parts.note: a bout is a fight or contest, as in boxing

explanation.surface: Someone worried about an upcoming match.
explanation.definitionFit: A book on a topic deals with or concerns it.

clue.text: Game to produce third-rate china?

parts.note: third-rate means poor or bad
Minton is a famous English porcelain manufacturer

explanation.surface: A sport supposedly turning out inferior porcelain.
explanation.walkthrough: Minton is a Staffordshire maker of fine bone china.
explanation.definitionFit: A racket sport played with a shuttlecock over a high net.

clue.text: Thought the Left quite the best

parts.note: an idea is a thought

explanation.surface: Left-wingers thought themselves perfect.
explanation.definitionFit: Perfect means the best imaginable.

clue.text: Disregard some sign, or eye it derisorily

indicators.note: some of the letters in the following words make up the answer

explanation.surface: Someone advised to pay no heed to a notice, or to look at it with scorn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' picks a run from 'sign, or eye'; 'it derisorily' only completes the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To pay no heed to something is to overlook it deliberately.

clue.text: They depend on horses for their sustenance

definitions.text: They depend on horses for their sustenance

parts.words: They depend on horses for their sustenance
parts.note: feed bags hang from horses' heads and hold their food, so they literally hang from horses for feeding

explanation.definitionFit: These canvas feed bags are hung over a horse's head to hold its fodder.

clue.text: Pleasant-sounding rock

indicators.note: the word for pleasant is said aloud to give the spelling of a rock

parts.note: pleasant means nice

explanation.surface: A stone that has an agreeable tone.
explanation.definitionFit: A banded metamorphic stone formed under heat and pressure.

clue.text: Personal support can make lots keen

indicators.note: these letters can be made into a different arrangement

explanation.surface: A personal helper can make many people enthusiastic.
explanation.definitionFit: The bony framework holds up a person's body.
